user_prompt:
Create a self-contained browser game called Dungeon Test.
Build a simple old-school first-person dungeon crawler based on a 10×10 grid of rooms. The player moves one room at a time using North, South, East and West buttons or the arrow keys.
Show the dungeon from the player’s first-person viewpoint. Do not display the complete 10×10 map. The scene should visibly change as the player moves and indicate walls or available directions.
Generate a valid, playable dungeon. The player must start in an open room with at least one possible move. Randomly place a treasure chest, monster and exit in separate reachable rooms. None may appear inside walls or on top of each other, and the dungeon must always be solvable.
Some movement directions should be blocked by walls. Attempting to move through a wall should leave the player in place and display a short message.
Show health, score and useful status messages. Finding the treasure increases the score and marks it as collected. The player may only win by reaching the exit after collecting the treasure.
Entering the monster room starts combat and presents Attack and Run controls. Attacking should damage the monster, with the monster able to damage the player in return. Defeating the monster ends combat. Running ends the encounter without defeating it. If player health reaches zero, show Game Over and allow a restart.
Make the interface responsive and use the available browser viewport, including full-screen display. Keep the graphics simple and procedural using only HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
Use no external assets, libraries, fonts or network resources. The finished game must run immediately in a modern browser.
